galleryNote.what: Any project may carry a `gallery` array of extra screens and clips, shown as a 'A closer look' section on its case study page. `image` stays the single cover shot used by cards and the case hero. Stills open full size in a lightbox; videos play inline.
galleryNote.galleryBase: Optional folder prefix. Set it once and every bare filename in `gallery` resolves against it, so a folder of screenshots costs one line each. Entries starting with http(s):// are left untouched, and entries starting with / are treated as site-root paths — both ignore the base.
galleryNote.types: `type` is optional. A src ending .mp4/.webm/.ogv/.mov is detected as a video; anything else is an image. Use "type": "youtube" or "vimeo" with an `id` for a hosted embed — those load lazily and YouTube is served from youtube-nocookie.com, so no cookie is set until a visitor presses play.
galleryNote.alt: Give every still an `alt`. It is the only description a screen-reader user gets, and the lightbox reuses it as the dialog title.

items.title: Advaith Homes
items.shortDescription: A comprehensive real estate platform built on WordPress with custom theme, plugins, and CPTs—20+ features including property management, calculators, expert profiles, and lead generation.
items.description: A fully custom WordPress platform for Advaith Homes that transforms how buyers discover, evaluate, and purchase properties. Built with a custom theme, specialized plugins, and custom post types that extend WordPress beyond its core capabilities—enabling the team to manage properties, experts, news, and leads through a familiar CMS interface.
highlights: Custom WordPress theme built from scratch for real estate workflows
Specialized plugins for property management, calculators, and lead routing
Custom Post Types: Properties, Experts, Tools, News, Reviews, Spotlights
3-level taxonomy filtering: Location → Property Type → Configuration
4 real estate calculator plugins: EMI, stamp duty, area converter, property tax
Dynamic popup system plugin with scheduling and behavioral triggers
Expert directory with custom profile fields and availability management
Application and inquiry forms with email automation and CRM integration
Property gallery system with unlimited images and lightbox
Review management with verification workflow and moderation queue
Mini spotlight CPT for construction progress videos
SEO optimization with Yoast integration and schema markup
Mobile-responsive design with 70% mobile traffic optimization

image.alt: Advaith Homes homepage: the property journey orbit linking budget, search, offer, survey, solicitor and completion stages

caseStudy.brief: Advaith Homes needed more than a property listing site—they needed an intelligent platform that educates buyers, provides decision-making tools, connects them with experts, and converts interest into applications. The challenge: build a comprehensive real estate ecosystem on WordPress that their team could manage daily through a familiar CMS interface, while delivering features that don't exist in any real estate plugin.
caseStudy.challenge:
Real estate buyers face information overload but lack clarity. They browse properties but can't calculate affordability. They need expert guidance but can't find the right consultant. Traditional real estate websites are either listing databases with poor UX or beautiful brochures with no substance. The client needed both: rich functionality with editorial flexibility.

WordPress real estate plugins offer listings but nothing else—no calculators, no expert management, no dynamic popups, no construction updates. Building everything as separate custom plugins while maintaining WordPress conventions meant reinventing the architecture without breaking the CMS paradigm. The platform had to serve multiple audiences—first-time buyers needing education, investors seeking tools, families wanting expert consultation—while the business team needed the familiar WordPress interface for daily content updates.
caseStudy.approach:
We architected the platform around WordPress core but extended it significantly through custom development. Instead of forcing generic plugins to fit, we built specialized solutions that leverage WordPress strengths while adding real estate-specific capabilities.

**Custom Post Types Architecture**: Properties, Experts, Tools, News, Reviews, Spotlights—each with custom fields through ACF Pro. Properties have 40+ custom fields (pricing, amenities, floor plans, RERA details). Experts have credentials, specializations, availability calendars. Reviews include verification workflow and moderation queues.

**Custom Taxonomy System**: Three-level hierarchical filtering (Location → Property Type → Configuration) using WordPress taxonomy system. Each location has property types, each type has configurations. Ajax-powered filtering updates available options dynamically—select "East Bangalore" and only apartment types in that area appear.

**Calculator Plugin Suite**: Four standalone plugins—EMI Calculator, Stamp Duty Estimator, Area Converter, Property Tax Calculator. Each integrates with property pages, saves calculation history, and feeds data to the lead system. Built as separate plugins for maintainability and potential reuse.

**Smart Popup Plugin**: Custom plugin for timed, behavioral, and exit-intent popups. Integrated with WordPress scheduling (start/end dates), frequency control (session/daily/weekly cookies), and conditional display rules (specific pages, user types, property categories).

**Expert Directory System**: Custom plugin managing consultant profiles, specializations, availability, booking calendar integration. Inquiry forms route to specific experts based on property interest and availability. Replaces generic contact forms with intelligent lead routing.

**Review Management Plugin**: Verification workflow where reviews submitted through forms enter a moderation queue. Admin can verify purchase (link to property transaction), approve/reject, mark as featured. Star ratings aggregate automatically. Property-specific and sitewide review displays.

**Gallery & Media Management**: Custom meta boxes for property images with categorization (exterior, interior, amenities, floorplans). Lightbox integration using WordPress media library. Video spotlights use custom CPT with featured thumbnails and play controls.

**Form Builder Integration**: Contact Form 7 extended with custom modules for property-specific inquiries, expert routing, calculation result submission. Each form triggers email automation and saves to lead database (custom table for reporting).

**Theme Architecture**: Custom theme built on Underscores (_s) starter, not a page builder. Template hierarchy for property archives, single properties, expert profiles, calculator pages, news archives. Mobile-first, accessible, performance-optimized.

**REST API Extensions**: Custom endpoints for property filtering, calculator results, expert availability checking. Enables Ajax filtering and live updates without page reloads.

**SEO Integration**: Yoast SEO extended with custom schema markup for properties (RealEstateAgent, Product types), reviews (Review schema), experts (Person schema). Automated breadcrumbs, XML sitemaps including all CPTs.
caseStudy.outcome:
A WordPress platform that goes far beyond standard real estate plugins. The team manages 45+ properties, expert profiles, news articles, and construction spotlights through the WordPress admin—familiar interface, exceptional functionality.

Application submissions increased as buyers arrive educated through calculator usage and pre-qualified by exploring properties systematically. The expert directory transformed from a static page into an engagement channel with direct expert routing based on property interest and specialization.

The plugin architecture delivered maintainability: each calculator is a standalone plugin, popup system is independent, review management is modular. Updates to one feature don't risk breaking others. Future reuse on other real estate projects becomes straightforward.

The custom theme provides full design control without page builder bloat. Template files are clean PHP, performance is optimized, and the mobile experience respects the 70% mobile traffic reality. No visual composer dependencies, no shortcode soup—just well-structured WordPress development.

Most importantly, the platform serves buyers the way they actually behave: they filter properties systematically, calculate affordability before calling, research the market through news, validate through reviews, and trust expert credentials before engaging. Every custom feature exists because WordPress alone couldn't deliver it, but the CMS remains familiar to the content team.
caseStudy.duration: 8 weeks design & development, 2 weeks content migration & QA

items.title: The Cane House
items.shortDescription: Freshly pressed sugarcane juice — online ordering and event catering, currently in build.
items.description: An online ordering and event catering site for a UK sugarcane juice brand. The holding page is live while the storefront is built: flavour ordering, and enquiry-to-booking for event catering.
highlights: Holding page live now — “Pressed Fresh. Served Cool.”
Event catering enquiry and booking flow

caseStudy._note: This project is still in build. The Outcome is deliberately empty — nothing to report until it ships. Replace the narrative with the real engagement story before publishing.
caseStudy.brief: A UK brand pressing sugarcane juice to order wanted to sell online and take event catering bookings, rather than relying on being found in person.
caseStudy.challenge: The product is made fresh and served cold, which makes it a poor fit for conventional shipping-based e-commerce. Ordering has to work around collection and events instead of a courier, and the catering side is an enquiry with a date and a headcount rather than an item in a basket.
caseStudy.approach: A holding page went up first so the brand had a working address while the storefront was built. Ordering is being modelled around flavours and collection rather than shipping, with event catering handled as a dated enquiry flow instead of a checkout — two different jobs that a single generic cart would do badly.
